caption: The grant covers the basics. The beadwork is what pays for everything else. Is that a normal split for anyone else?

slides.title:
How I live on
my R6 800
p/m income
Living in Bizana
slides.body:
Female, 36
Living with two children (14 and 9)
Income: Disability grant plus beadwork sold at church markets
Net income: R6 800 p/m (this month)

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Maize meal, vegetables, the basics for the three of us
slides.body: I plan this one first. Everything else fits around whatever's left of it.

slides.title: School uniform & stationery
slides.includes: Shoes for the older one, exercise books for both
slides.body: The school doesn't ask why it's late. It still means I have to find it somewhere.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to town on market days to sell and to restock beads
slides.body: If I don't get to the market, there's no beadwork money that week. Simple as that.

slides.title: Beadwork materials
slides.includes: Beads, thread, wire from the craft supplier in town
slides.body: People pay R80 for a piece that costs me R25 to make. The rest is my time, which doesn't show up on a statement.

slides.title: Funeral policy
slides.includes: Cover for myself and both children
slides.body: This one comes off no matter what. I decided that a long time ago.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, airtime & data, stokvel, soap and toiletries
slides.body: Small amounts, but there are five of them and they all want to go first.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R6 800. R150 some months, nothing in others. The beadwork is what makes the difference.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I use Money Rhythm to check in on the grant and the beadwork money on the days I actually have signal, so I can see the two together instead of guessing.

No bank login needed.
